_comment: Curated alarm-name -> citation registry read by scripts/check_alarm_citations.py (#1959). Every CloudWatch alarm that has been in ALARM >72h must have an entry here (exact AlarmName key) naming the incident row or issue that explains it, or the /wrap gate flags it by name. Since #2912 the same holds for an alarm that FIRED AND CLEARED within the last 72h (episode start and end both in-window, read from describe-alarm-history) — a flap between wraps is invisible to current-state duration by construction, so it needs an entry or an explicit --decoded line just like a standing red. Add an entry the same session a new long-red alarm (or flap) is triaged; remove/replace one once the underlying issue closes AND the alarm has actually cleared live.

token-alarm-genesis-window-active.note: NOT A FAULT — by design. This is a boolean gauge sub-alarm carrying NO SNS action of its own (cdk/stacks/monitoring_stack.py, the TokenAlarmGenesisWindowActive block). ALARM means literally 'we are inside the genesis window', which the two composite alarms combine with the token-threshold breach so a genesis-week breach is digested rather than paged (#2116, after #1961's post-genesis rebuild pages). Cycle 13's genesis is 2026-08-10, so red since 2026-08-07 is the correct state. Expected to return to OK when the window closes; treat_missing_data=NOT_BREACHING so a stale gauge can never silently suppress a real page. If it is still ALARM well after the genesis window ends, THAT is the finding — file it, don't re-cite.

cost-metric-drift-sustained.note: Expected RED from ~7 days after its first deploy: the alarm states a true, known condition. CostMetricDriftRatio has held ~1.37 since 2026-08-19 (measured live, #2883's 2026-08-20 comment) against the 1.15 acceptance bar — the residual self-report undercount (#2883 box 2: un-instrumented Bedrock callers outside Lambda, e.g. CI runners without AWS_LAMBDA_FUNCTION_NAME, plus partial cache-token capture) is still open. The alarm exists precisely so this residual cannot rot silently the way #357's regression did. Remove this entry when box 2 lands the ratio < 1.15 for a full week AND the alarm has actually cleared live.

budget-tier-sustained-7d.note: Re-measured 2026-08-22 by executing the shipped cost_governor `_tier_for`, superseding the 2026-08-15 note here — which had rotted when #2836 made the base permanent (it still cited a $135 ceiling reverting to $85/$100; both numbers are wrong). THE PROJECTION HALF IS RESOLVED, NO OVERRUN: mtd $124.80, projected $162.60 against the $200 August ceiling = 81%. September at the measured $4.05/day run rate projects $121.50 against the permanent $150 base = 81% — also under. Neither month overruns, so the accept/cut/extend trilemma the issue posed has no live premise. WHAT REMAINS IS THE ALARM'S CUT, not the spend: ADR-133 derived the $150 base from a measured steady state of $4.12/day, and $4.12 x 30 = $123.60 = 82.4% of $150, which is INSIDE band 1 (73-87%). So the ceiling was set from a run rate that sits in band 1 by construction, and this alarm — which fires when the tier never returns to 0 across a week — alarms on the designed steady state. Band 0 would require daily spend at or under $3.66. Tracked for re-cut; remove this entry when the alarm clears or its threshold moves.

weekly-signal-delivery-heartbeat.note: Arming transient, 2026-08-22: the alarm landed with treat_missing=BREACHING and no datapoints, so it entered ALARM on creation and cleared the moment the seed datapoint was written (1 fire / 1 clear). Expected on any missing-data-breaching heartbeat's first minutes; a REAL missed Wednesday send is a 7-day Sum<1 breach, not a flap. Re-cite if it flaps again after a real send cycle.

qa-smoke-failures.note: Flap 2026-08-22 (1 fire / 1 clear): the content-truth smoke findings this session's #2939/#2941 fixes were draining. Non-gating by #1921's posture; the count fell as fixes propagated.

qa-smoke-warnings.note: 35 fires / 35 clears in the 72h window — NOT 35 distinct failures. #2912 measured the mechanism: the Period=86400 alarm evaluates a sliding 24h window every minute, so a fresh datapoint flickers in and out of the aggregate for ~2.5h, flapping the state. The flap detector that reports this is #2912's own; the underlying organic WarnCount>=1 emissions are #1921's non-gating content-truth class.

ingest-liveness-unhealthy.note: FLAP, not a standing red (#2912 detector caught it 2026-08-22). Fired and cleared inside one 72h window, so current-state duration is structurally blind to it. Investigated live this session: UnhealthySourceCount last landed a datapoint on 2026-08-20 while pipeline-health-check logged '16 pass, 0 fail' 2.2h before the wrap — the alarm was lit on a two-day-old datapoint describing a state the producer no longer reports. Root cause is the #2976 class: Period=86400 with the metric emitted only on the unhealthy path, so the alarm cannot fall as fast as the system recovers. Remove this entry when #2976 lands the healthy-path emission AND re-cuts the period; if it flaps again BEFORE that, the flap count is the signal — do not re-cite, add it to #2976 as evidence.
